newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican President to visit United States.
newsitem.headline: Mexican President to visit United States.

text.p: Mexican leader Ernesto Zedillo travels to the United States on Monday for a three-day trip ahead of President Bill Clinton's own visit to Mexico a week later, officials said on Sunday.
Zedillo will leave Mexico early on Monday for Atlanta to attend a conference later in the day at the Carter Centre for Latin American Affairs, the presidents' office said in a statement.
On Tuesday, he is scheduled to take part in a CNN World Contributors Conference, to be broadcast by the Atlanta-based cable television network.
U.N. Secretary General Kofi Anan, Georgia Gov. Zell Miller and CNN head Ted Turner are slated to attend a lunch in Zedillo's honour later in the day, the statement said.
Zedillo, who took office in 1994 after replacing slain ruling party candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio, returns to Mexico on Wednesday.

Clinton is scheduled to visit Mexico from May 5-7 in a visit that is largely seen as a goodwill gesture after recent tensions between both nations over Mexico's inability to stop the flow of illegal drugs to the United States.
